decisions.decision: Use a lightweight engineering continuity control plane: project control plan, AI organisation model, handoff, work state, decision ledger, assumption ledger and drift checks.
decisions.reason: The repository already has strong technical documentation but needs durable cross-session state and explicit drift controls. Project Athena demonstrates useful structural patterns for this problem, but its identity/institutional model is not appropriate to copy into a Minecraft development platform.
evidence: Project Athena AI-PORTAL.md separates source-of-truth layers, capability state and cross-agent context.
Project Athena agents/agent-registry.yml uses explicit roles, authority and capabilities.
Project Athena audit/decision-framework.md records evidence, falsification and rollback.
This repository already uses R0-R6 readiness and evidence-aware AI instructions.
decisions.review_trigger: Major repository architecture change or replacement of the AI continuity system
decisions.rollback: Remove the added control files and restore the prior AGENTS/AI_HANDOFF/context-map references if the model proves burdensome or contradictory.

decisions.decision: Do not perform a full old-brand scrub until a replacement brand is selected and its canonical spelling/slug/prefix are frozen.
decisions.reason: A partial rename would create more terminology drift and could corrupt protocol/ABI or persisted-data identifiers that require migration handling.
evidence: The previous brand appears across documentation, workflow names, code identifiers and the VFSB/native bridge vocabulary.
Superseded by DEC-2026-08-28-004 after Gridelyx was selected.
decisions.rollback: Not applicable; its gating condition has been satisfied.

decisions.decision: The platform is not limited to conventional mod-loader extension points. Requirements may escalate through loader transforms, JVM instrumentation, native components, sidecars, launch/bootstrap changes, deterministic executable/library patches or project-owned runtime components when shallower integration cannot provide the required capability. Deep changes remain additive, version/fingerprint gated, attributable and reversible.
decisions.reason: The product goal is a creator/development platform rather than a conventional mod. Treating frozen registries, non-public engine behavior, executable boundaries or loader APIs as absolute product limits would incorrectly weaken requirements. The safer engineering model is to preserve a verified upstream base and layer project-owned capability through explicit patch/overlay/component graphs with rollback.
evidence: Explicit human direction allows patching the game/executable or adding components when required, provided changes are additive.
Existing architecture already includes JVM agents, bytecode transformation, native/IPC components, sidecars, virtual registries and process isolation.
docs/DEEP_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md defines the escalation ladder, immutable-base rule, patch manager and drift policy.
decisions.review_trigger: Any L5-L8 integration, upstream executable/library change, security-boundary change or discovery that a shallower stable integration can fully replace a deeper patch
decisions.rollback: Disable the affected patch/component capability, restore the verified base artifact or prior patch graph, and fall back to the last-known-good shallower integration where available.

decisions.decision: Adopt Gridelyx as the canonical root brand and Gridelyx Studio as the integrated suite name. New project-owned identifiers and documentation use Gridelyx. Existing Gridelyx/VFSB source, ABI, protocol and persisted identifiers are treated as explicit migration debt and must change through versioned compatibility work rather than blind replacement.
decisions.reason: The human project owner selected Gridelyx after candidate exploration. Freezing the identity now removes naming ambiguity while preserving technical compatibility during the staged migration.
evidence: Explicit human selection: Gridelyx is the approved replacement root brand.
Ordinary web/GitHub screening found no obvious exact-name collision at selection time; this is not legal trademark clearance.
platform/brand.json schema version 2 records the canonical identity and compatibility identifiers.
docs/REBRAND_PLAN.md defines the staged migration and exit criteria.
decisions.review_trigger: Legal/trademark conflict, human-directed rename, or discovery that a frozen technical identifier must use a different compatibility namespace
decisions.rollback: Pause public migration, preserve compatibility aliases and update platform/brand.json plus the rebrand decision before any further source/ABI changes.

decisions.decision: Adopt CR-034 Feature Decision Packets as the standard analysis process for substantial Gridelyx features and architecture. The process combines W5x5x5 positive/inverse interrogation, task decomposition, project values, cost and multi-horizon diagnostics, opportunity cost, regret/reversibility, risk/inversion/pre-mortem, second-order analysis, Eisenhower, overlap/Venn analysis, first principles, verified benchmarking, Feynman explanation, MVP/timeboxing, asymmetric risk, working backward, Pareto, Critical Path, Cynefin, Kanban, evidence and rollback.
decisions.reason: Gridelyx has many interacting long-horizon capabilities across launcher, loaders, Java/Bedrock, world mutation, rendering, physics, AI, native code and production. A repeatable decision packet makes hidden assumptions, dependencies, failure modes, shared primitives and long-term effects explicit while preserving ambitious retained scope.
evidence: Explicit human direction requested the W5x5x5 and named decision/risk/planning frameworks as a standard feature-analysis model.
docs/FEATURE_DECISION_FRAMEWORK.md defines the complete method.
platform/feature-analysis.schema.json provides a machine-readable contract.
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature-evaluation.yml provides contributor intake.
tools/feature_planning_check.py and Gridelyx continuity CI enforce structural preservation.
decisions.review_trigger: The framework becomes materially burdensome, misses recurring failure classes, or a human-directed replacement methodology is accepted
decisions.rollback: Retain existing Feature Decision Packets as historical evidence, replace the schema/process through an explicit decision, and update CR-034 plus AI/community/CI references coherently.

decisions.decision: Keep the canonical product/API identity as Gridelyx/gridelyx while using the explicitly requested GitHub repository slug gridlyx. Target repository full name is IAMACESIRX/gridlyx with the combined Gridelyx and Minecraft Advanced Mod Development Kit description recorded in platform/repository-metadata.json.
decisions.reason: The human project owner explicitly requested the repository be renamed to gridlyx after Gridelyx had already been frozen as the product identity. Separating product identity from repository slug preserves both instructions without silently changing the product namespace.
evidence: Explicit human request for repository name gridlyx and combined description.
platform/repository-metadata.json records the requested target and current blocked state.
GitHub Issue #28 tracks the actual repository metadata mutation and validation.
decisions.review_trigger: Repository metadata is successfully migrated, GitHub reports a collision, or the human owner changes either product or repository naming
decisions.rollback: Do not rewrite Git history. If the repository rename fails or is reversed, update repository metadata/remotes/links while retaining Gridelyx as product/API identity unless separately changed.
